key_insight: Light can reversibly switch halide ions in 2D mixed-halide perovskites through intrinsic light-lattice coupling, not defects, enabling a defect-free photo-switching mechanism that resets when illumination is removed.
engineering_relevance: This points to a route for stable, reversible optoelectronic devices and photoswitchable materials where optical response can be tuned on demand without permanent structural damage.
method: Nudged elastic band calculations to map the halide-exchange energy barrier.
Photo-force calculations to quantify light-induced non-equilibrium driving work.
GW-based optical calculations plus phonon/electron-phonon analysis to connect spectra, bandgap renormalization, and soft-mode dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement between GW-calculated absorption spectra and experiments in the dark, along with a light-induced redshift consistent with bandgap renormalization and reversible halide swapping.
watch_item: The mechanism relies on illumination-driven non-equilibrium forces that only partially overcome the activation barrier, so switching performance may depend strongly on light intensity and material-specific phonon coupling.
paper_title: Reversible photo-switching optical functionality in two-dimensional mixed-halide hybrid perovskites
